← SOLSTICE PROJECT NOTES

Honda oil-pan and baffle precedents

Research refreshed 2026-10-14. These sources expand the architecture comparison for the Solstice study; none supplies a dimensioned Solstice interface, a transferable baffle outline, or proof of oil-control performance in the LNF pan. Patent and paper figures are schematic unless explicitly stated. Product dimensions below describe complete Honda-family pans unless stated otherwise.

OEM and aftermarket construction

S2000 OEM parts catalog

Honda's S2000 parts catalog, sheet E-14 (S2A1-E1400B), lists oil pan 11200-PCX-000 and a separate baffle plate 11221-PCX-000. The parts list names the latter “PLATE, BAFFLE.” This confirms a distinct fixed OEM plate in that assembly, but the exploded view is not a dimensioned drawing and does not establish its internal flow features or shape at useful scale. The original Honda-hosted catalog and parts list were discoverable through indexing; direct PDF retrieval returned HTTP 403 during this review.

RisingTuning K-series bolt-in baffle

The product listing specifies 1.5 mm 5052-H32 aluminum and six studs, spacers, washers and nuts. Its pictured plate divides the pan area into three regions and retains open paths around the pickup/return area. It is specified for K20A/A2/Z1 pump-and-pan configurations, with stated exclusions and conversion requirements for some K20/K24 applications. No plan dimensions or independently measured performance are published. This supports comparing a fixed, removable, three-zone plate with hinged collectors; its material and thickness remain that product's data only. Manufacturer listing

Honda CBR600 FSAE oil-pan study — fixed baffle comparison

Zha Yunfei, Zhang Lihao, Liao Yuhui, Qian Renhuan, Zeng Xinlong, and Zhong Yong, “Improved design of oil pan for Honda CBR600 engine based on FSC,” *Journal of Fujian University of Technology* 15(4), 2017, pp. 324–327, journal record and DOI, official PDF.

  • Printed p. 325, section 2 and Figs. 1–2: the authors redesigned the complete pan and compared four reinforced floor plates in rectangular and diamond layouts. The baffle positions are shown schematically; no plate dimensions, datums, or Solstice interfaces are supplied.
  • Printed p. 325, VOF setup: the model used 1.5 g longitudinal and lateral acceleration, 45 mm baffles selected relative to that engine's pickup height, and an oil level 10 mm above the baffles. These are inputs for that CBR600 pan simulation, not OEM specifications, validated Solstice loads, or recommended insert dimensions.
  • Printed p. 326, Figs. 5–6 and Table 1: the paper reports less simulated interface motion and less oil displaced from the pickup for its diamond layout. Its table gives 2.2 L capacity for both pans, 825 g versus 833 g mass, and 137 mm versus 77 mm height. The abstract separately reports a 59 mm center-of-gravity reduction although the tabulated heights differ by 60 mm; retain both statements as published rather than reconciling them.
  • Printed p. 327, section 5: the authors report 65.9–237.0 kPa bench pressure, 62.8–226.5 kPa road-test pressure, and nearly 1,000 km of testing and racing with the modified-pan prototype. These are reported whole-system outcomes, not a controlled rectangular-versus-diamond pressure test and not evidence for the Solstice LNF.

This is the strongest new Honda example for comparing a fixed-wall architecture with the current gated concepts. It justifies keeping rectangular/diamond fixed partitions in the design-option register, but it does not support copying the Honda plate height, oil-level offset, layout coordinates, or results into Solstice geometry. A Solstice fixed-wall option would need its own declared envelope and fit checks.

Moroso S2000 weld-in trap-door baffle — service sequence

Moroso's P/N 23040 installation instructions identify one welded aluminum subassembly for the F20/F22 S2000 pan. The sheet says the subassembly self-aligns in the pan, describes tack then stitch welding, and instructs the installer to verify every swing door moves freely before cleaning and reinstalling the pan. It gives no dimensions. This is a useful service/inspection precedent for a permanently installed race baffle, not geometry or a recommended attachment method for the removable Solstice insert.

Adjacent-engine windage and aeration references

These sources concern an upper crank/windage layer rather than the lower Solstice pickup insert. They are recorded to keep the two functions and their clearances separate.

  • Toyota/Soken patent US8210149B2, “Baffle plate”, Figs. 7A–7B, describes a guide groove shaped around a crank counterweight and a gap of approximately 9 mm between them. This is an application-specific moving-crank clearance for an upper return/windage plate, not a pickup, cover, or Solstice insert clearance.
  • Bridget A. Baran, *Engine Lubrication Oil Aeration*, MIT S.M. thesis, 2007, studies a motored Ford 3.0 L V6. Printed p. 51 reports a 5 mm windage-tray-to-counterweight spacing; pp. 57–58 and Table 4-3 vary mesh construction/open area; pp. 61–64 report no significant aeration change from those open-area substitutions within the instrument tolerance and tested conditions. Those values are specific to that engine and test. They caution against treating mesh openness alone as an oil-control or aeration prediction.

Additional source-checked dimensions and architectures

  • The text of Honda patent US7748500B2, Fig. 4, describes a gap “on the order of 0.5 mm” at the seam between upper and lower portions of one split baffle wall. This is the only useful explicit gap dimension found in this second pass. It is a detail of that integrated Honda pan, not a door clearance, Solstice target, tolerance, or recommended design value. It is useful only as a reminder to keep split-wall seams explicit in a future concept comparison.
  • The 2000–08 S2000 service manual reproduction shows the separate baffle in the component index (printed p. 8-3 / PDF p. 253) and pan removal/installation context (printed pp. 7-10 and 7-25). Those illustrations have no scale or baffle dimensions.
  • WO2012035426A1, “Oil pan inner tank valve structure” shows a buoyant disc valve guided between inner and outer oil-pan tanks. It adds a level-responsive, two-reservoir architecture to the broad comparison set, but its seat, guide, buoyancy and tank interfaces are unlike a removable Solstice insert and have no transferable dimensions. It is not a current candidate.
  • A reseller listing for Honda baffle 11221-PCX-000 supplies 11.6 × 7.9 × 1.4 in “item dimensions,” but does not give a drawing, datums, source method or measurement trace. Do not use these as a verified part envelope. Honda's own S2000 catalog confirms the part identity but does not provide metric geometry.

Implications for the current A/B/C study

  • Keep the earlier fixed-divider concept as a meaningful zero-hinge comparator; Honda's S2000 catalog identity and K-series bolt-in construction support the architecture class, not Solstice dimensions.
  • Treat the windage/upper-return layer separately from the lower pickup collector. Existing Solstice cover geometry is still only an image-informed proxy.
  • Keep the Honda CBR600 fixed rectangular/diamond baffle comparison available as a possible new style, but do not copy its 45 mm baffle height, 10 mm oil-level offset, plate coordinates, or system results. A Solstice fixed-wall model would need independently declared dimensions and scenario checks.
  • The Moroso S2000 installation note supports checking every moving leaf for free swing after assembly; it does not validate this project's custom hinge or imply a weld-in attachment.
  • Do not use the Toyota 9 mm counterweight gap or Ford 5 mm windage-tray gap as a clearance target for the lower Solstice insert. A crank/windage layer is a separate concept and needs its own crank-motion geometry and oil-return path.
  • Model the pickup, its support/opening, return direction, and attachment pattern as coupled interfaces. A visually clear opening is not a verified fit.
  • Keep pump/pickup compatibility, upper plate, pan depth, fasteners, and installation sequence in the scenario register. Honda package variations show why one part's envelope cannot be transferred by engine-family name.
  • The current A/B/C gate geometries are not changed by these analogies. Any future static plate or return-channel variant should be a new explicit concept with its own saved solids and checks, not a relabeling of a Honda design.

Evidence boundary

Product, patent, and paper descriptions are architecture references. The Canton values are pan-level dimensions transcribed from its catalog and converted to millimetres for comparison. Honda parts-catalog item identities establish that a separate plate exists in the S2000 assembly; they do not reveal its metric geometry. The Honda manual, Moroso installation instructions, CBR600 paper figures, and patent illustrations do not provide a dimensioned Solstice insert drawing. The 0.5 mm Honda split-wall seam and CBR600 study's 45 mm baffle/10 mm oil-level offset are application-specific examples, not Solstice targets. The Toyota 9 mm and Ford 5 mm values refer to crank/windage clearances in other engines. No source here reduces the unknown Solstice interior, pickup, cover, mount, or placement parameters.
